'''Henry Keith Moffatt''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] (born 12 April 1935) is a British mathematician with research interests in the field of [[fluid dynamics]], particularly [[magnetohydrodynamics]] and the theory of [[turbulence]]. He was Professor of Mathematical Physics at the [[University of Cambridge]] from 1980 to 2002.

==Early life and education==
Moffatt was born on 12 April 1935 to Emmeline Marchant and Frederick Henry Moffatt''.''<ref name=":0">{{Citation|chapter=Moffatt, Prof. (Henry) Keith, (born 12 April 1935), Professor of Mathematical Physics, University of Cambridge, 1980–2002, now Professor Emeritus (Head of Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, 1983–91); Fellow, Trinity College, Cambridge, 1961–76, and since 1980|date=2007-12-01|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-27771|publisher=Oxford University Press|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.u27771|access-date=2019-05-04|title=Who's Who|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was schooled at [[George Watson's College]], Edinburgh, going on to study Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Edinburgh]], graduating in 1957. He then went to [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he studied mathematics and, 1959, he was a [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Wrangler]]. In 1960, he was awarded a [[Smith's Prize]] while preparing his PhD degree.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hkm2/PDFs/HKM_CV.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|date=July 2022}}</ref> He received his doctorate in 1962; his dissertation, ''Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence'', was supervised by [[George Batchelor]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|50419}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing his doctorate, Moffatt joined the staff of the Mathematics Faculty at the [[University of Cambridge]] as an Assistant Lecturer<ref name=":0" /> and became a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]]. He was appointed a lecturer in 1964, and held the office of Tutor, then Senior Tutor, at Trinity between 1970 and 1976.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080229132236/http://www.newton.cam.ac.uk/keith_biog.html|url=http://www.newton.cam.ac.uk/keith_biog.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2008-02-29|title=Professor Keith Moffatt FRS|publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref>

In 1977, he was appointed to the Chair of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name=":0" /> He held this position until 1980 when he returned to Cambridge to take up the Chair in Mathematical Physics, renewing his Fellowship of Trinity College. In 2002, he was made an Emeritus Professor of the University (he remains a Fellow of Trinity).<ref name=cv/>

He held the ''Chaire Internationale de Recherche Blaise Pascal'' at the [[École Normale Supérieure]], Paris, from 2001 to 2003, and was [[Leverhulme Trust|Leverhulme]] Professor, from 2003 to 2005. He was president of the [[International Union of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics]] from 2000 to 2004.<ref name=cv/>

==Honours and awards==
Moffatt was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1986;<ref name=rs>{{citation|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/keith-moffatt-11967/|title=Keith Moffatt|work=Fellows directory|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=2025-05-23}}</ref> [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1988;<ref name=cv/> Foreign Member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1991;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/leden/moffatt|title=Keith Moffatt |language=nl |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=2025-05-23}}</ref> [[Member of Academia Europæa]] in 1994; Foreign Member of the [[Académie des Sciences]], Paris, in 1998; Foreign Member of the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]], Rome, in 2001; Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2003; and a foreign associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2008.<ref name=cv/>

He became an ''officier'' in the ''[[Ordre des Palmes académiques]]'' in 1998. He received the Panetti-Ferrari International Prize and Gold Medal of the [[Academy of Sciences of Turin]] in 2001, the Euromech Prize for Fluid Mechanics in 2003,<ref name=cv/> the Caribbean Award for Fluid Dynamics in 2004,<ref name=rs/> the [[Senior Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2005,<ref name=cv/> and the [[Hughes Medal]] of the [[Royal Society]] in 2005.<ref name=rs/>

== Personal life ==
In 1960, he married Katharine (Linty), and together they had four children, two daughters and two sons, one of whom is deceased.<ref name=":0" />
